title: Calling all vibecoders and devs…
author: EffectNo2152
selftext:
**Let’s make a Frankenstein game.**

Everybody works in the same repo. No grand vision. No single engine/style/tool requirement beyond whatever we can reasonably glue together.

You’re good at Blender? Add some weird assets.

Godot/Unity/Three.js/web dev? Build a mechanic.

Pixel artist? Make a UI.

Music/SFX? Add it.

AI/vibecoder who barely knows what the hell they’re doing? Perfect. Make something and submit it.

The idea is that everybody contributes **whatever they have** and we keep stitching it together until we somehow end up with a playable game.

One shared repo. Branches/PRs so we don’t immediately destroy it. 

Very few creative rules. If somebody adds a fishing minigame and somebody else adds a mech and somebody else builds a haunted gas station, now those things exist in the same universe and we figure out how to connect them.

Basically open-source game development as an exquisite corpse.

**First contribution:** fork the repo, add one small thing, and open a pull request. It can be a mechanic, asset, sound, room, character, item, dumb joke, whatever. Don’t overthink it — just add one piece to the monster.

**No idea what the final game is. That’s the point.**

Who wants in?

https://github.com/jalapenoseed/frankenstein-game

replies.author: BlahajWithBenefits

Enforce size limits on what people contribute. I.e a small mechanic, asset, feature, whatever.

That way AI and humans can more easily review it and its harder to hide anything malicious.

Still a risk but one thats been managed in open source stuff plenty of times.
